question: Who is the most blessed woman?
summary: Gabriel tells Mary in Luke 1:28 that she is 'blessed among women.' The Song of Deborah (Judg 5:24) calls Jael 'blessed above women' for driving a tent peg through Sisera's skull. Judith 13:18 calls Judith 'blessed above all women on the earth' for decapitating Holofernes. Three texts each elevate a different woman to the superlative of female blessedness.

reconcile.connective: Defenders read "blessed among/above women" as a relative, comparative idiom of honor — not an exclusive cosmic ranking — so the same praise can fall on Jael, Judith, and Mary without conflict.

discrepancy.connective: Steve Wells (Skeptics Annotated Bible) presses the wording directly, noting that Jael and Judith are blessed "above" all women while Mary is only blessed "among" them, so the three superlatives cannot all hold.

pd_work.note: Treats this passage directly, reading Mary's 'blessed among women' as a relative honor 'in external distinction' and explicitly subordinating it to the Lord's own redefinition of blessedness, which resolves the competing-superlatives objection. Haley's coverage of this specific minor row is unconfirmed, so anchored to a harmonizing commentator surfaced on the row, per the policy's 'also acceptable' provision.

excerpts.excerpt_text: As the mother of our Lord, she was the most "blessed among women" in external distinction; but let them listen to the Lord's own words. "Nay, rather blessed are they that hear the word of God and keep it."
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Directly relativizes Mary's superlative: she is most blessed 'in external distinction' only, with the real blessing redefined — treats 'blessed among women' as a qualified, non-exclusive honor, dissolving the competition with Jael/Judith.
excerpts.source_note_text: highly favoured--a word only once used elsewhere (Eph 1:6, "made accepted"): compare Luk 1:30, "Thou hast found favour with God." The mistake of the Vulgate's rendering, "full of grace," has been taken abundant advantage of by the Romish Church. As the mother of our Lord, she was the most "blessed among women" in external distinction; but let them listen to the Lord's own words. "Nay, rather blessed are they that hear the word of God and keep it." (See on Luk 11:27).
